# Playbook: SaaS Web App

A multi-user software product sold (or given away) as a service: accounts, a database, a web UI, and usually subscription billing. This is the default playbook — when no other playbook matches a project type on at least two of (payments? accounts? content-led or app-led?), use this one (§5.6 closest-match rule; ties go to SaaS).

## Goal

Ship a production SaaS: real accounts and tenant isolation, a tested API and schema, subscription billing verified in test mode before any live key is touched, WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility, and a monitored deployment with a proven rollback — with zero critical security findings and every QA gate green.

## Departments and order

D1 → D2+D7 → D3+D13+D4+D5 → D11 → D7+D8 → D6 → D9 — exactly as the §5.6 table; no deviation. D12 and D14 appear as explicit steps 5 and 6 per the §5.6 standing rule (they are not in the table's order string); D17 and D18 appear as conditional steps 4b and 6b.

## Docs to write first

Before any code, scaffold from `project-templates` and write:

- `requirements.md` — the requirement set with priorities and acceptance criteria (D1).
- `fact-sheet.md` — every public claim, price, and plan name the product will make, with sources (D1). Prices here must mirror the billing configuration (G-PR-063).
- `stack.md` — the chosen stack and the criteria that chose it, recorded before the choice is final (G-AR-023).
- `progress.md` — session log, gate results, blockers; updated every session (§5.10).
- `DECISIONS.md` — architecture decisions and any skill conflicts resolved under §5.7 precedence.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — containers, data ownership, failure behavior (step 2 output, started now as a stub).
- `SCHEMA.md` — data invariants the schema gates check against (step 3).
- `SECURITY.md` — threat model summary and the OWASP checklist record (step 2, completed at step 7).
- `.env.example` — every secret by name + purpose, no values (§5.9).

## Step-by-step sequence

**Step 0 — Core and scaffold.** Load `bundles/core.md`. Generate the project from `project-templates` (gate G-PM-001 manifest diff, G-PM-002 unreplaced-token scan). Write the docs above. Load `secrets-management` now — every later step that needs a key follows §5.9.

**Step 1 — Requirements (D1).** Run `requirements-writing`: requirements with testable acceptance criteria, a named Must set, and an explicit out-of-scope list. Populate `fact-sheet.md` with every claim and price the marketing surface will repeat.
◆ **DECISION — is billing actually in scope?** If the product is free with no paid tier, drop step 4 and record the drop in `requirements.md` ("Dropped, with reason") and `DECISIONS.md` (§6.3 step 5). Never build a dormant checkout. (Unattended run: BOOTSTRAP's approval-points rule applies at this point — a decision recorded in the commissioning brief or `requirements.md` counts as the answer; if none is recorded and no user is reachable, follow the §6.3 stuck protocol (log-and-continue, then the safe defaults) and record the substitution in `progress.md`.)

**Step 2 — Architecture + security design (D2+D7).** Run `system-design` (containers, data ownership, failure behavior) and `threat-modelling` in the same pass — the design is not final until the threat model has been read against it. Record stack choice in `stack.md` with criteria dated before the decision (G-AR-023).
◆ **DECISION — single-tenant or multi-tenant?** If more than one customer organization will share the database, `tenant-isolation` and `multitenancy-saas` are mandatory in step 3, not optional. (Unattended run: BOOTSTRAP's approval-points rule applies at this point — a decision recorded in the commissioning brief or `requirements.md` counts as the answer; if none is recorded and no user is reachable, follow the §6.3 stuck protocol (log-and-continue, then the safe defaults) and record the substitution in `progress.md`.)

**Step 3 — Build (D3+D13+D4+D5).** Build in this internal order: schema first (invariants in `SCHEMA.md`, migrations reversible), API second (contract-first, `api-building`), auth and authorization with the API (`backend-auth`, `rbac`), throttling shipped with the auth surface (`rate-limiting` — login, signup, and password-reset endpoints are rate-limited from this step, not retrofitted after a review finding), UI last against the real API — never against mock data that hides API gaps. D13 runs inside this step, not after it: tokens pass the contrast script (G-AC-011) before components are built on them, and every screen is built to the WCAG 2.2 AA criterion checklist (G-AC-015).

**Step 4 — Billing (D11).** ◆ **STOP AND ASK — no payment provider chosen (§6.3 step 4).** If `requirements.md` names no provider, stop and ask with concrete options (e.g. "Option A: Stripe — subscription tooling and test clocks; Option B: defer billing and ship the free tier only"). Do not pick a provider silently and do not build against a guessed one. Then: request **test-mode keys only** via the §5.9 handoff; build checkout, subscription lifecycle, and webhook handling; verify with the test-clock lifecycle walk (G-IN-011) and the webhook forgery test (G-IN-051). (Unattended run: BOOTSTRAP's approval-points rule applies at this point — a decision recorded in the commissioning brief or `requirements.md` counts as the answer; if none is recorded and no user is reachable, follow the §6.3 stuck protocol (log-and-continue, then the safe defaults) and record the substitution in `progress.md`.)
**Step 4b — AI features (D17, conditional).** Only if the product has AI features: `llm-integration` (provider SDK contained behind one wrapper, G-AI-001) and `ai-safety` (red-team injection suite, G-AI-021) become part of the build, and their gates join the step 7 list.

**Step 5 — Performance budgets (D12, explicit step).** Set the budget file with `performance-budgets` before the verification phase: per-route budgets asserted in CI (G-AN-101), budget file linted (G-AN-102). A budget written after the first failing measurement is a waiver, not a budget — record it as one.

**Step 6 — Legal and privacy (D14, explicit step).** Build the processing register and data map (`privacy-laws`), draft Terms/Privacy from the register — never from a template copied off another product — and wire cookie consent so nothing non-essential fires before consent (G-LG-041). The published documents must diff clean against the register (G-LG-031). Data-subject capability is gated in this step, not assumed: the DSAR drill (G-LG-021, `dsar-handling`) runs an access request and an erasure request through the real product flow, so account deletion and data export must exist as working capabilities — self-serve, or a documented request path running on the LG-043 response clock — before this step can pass.
**Step 6b — Support surfaces (D18, conditional).** Only if the product ships help/support: `support-ticketing` intake end-to-end test (G-CX-001) and `user-onboarding` fresh-account walkthrough (G-CX-031) join the gate list.

**Step 7 — Verification (D7+D8).** Full OWASP pass (`owasp` checklist review G-SE-003, ZAP baseline G-SE-001), secrets scan over full git history (G-SE-041), dependency vulnerability gate (G-SE-051), placeholder scan (G-QA-141), end-to-end suite green on the preview deployment (G-QA-021), and the qa-gates meta-checks (G-QA-111 negative control, G-QA-113 waiver/provenance check). **No deployment step starts until every gate in this step passes.**

**Step 8 — Deploy (D6, last build step).** CI/CD pipeline with the broken-test drill proven (G-DO-001), hosting checks against the real production domain (G-DO-071 external production check, G-DO-073 exposure probe), rollback drill in staging before the first production deploy (G-DO-151), monitoring and alerts live (`reliability`).
◆ **STOP AND ASK — go-live switch (§5.9 step 6).** Switching from test to live payment keys, purging test data, and re-pointing webhooks requires the user's explicit approval. The agent prepares the checklist; the user approves the switch. (Unattended run: BOOTSTRAP's approval-points rule applies at this point — a decision recorded in the commissioning brief or `requirements.md` counts as the answer; if none is recorded and no user is reachable, follow the §6.3 stuck protocol (log-and-continue, then the safe defaults) and record the substitution in `progress.md`.)

**Step 9 — Launch surface (D9).** Indexability verified on the production routes (G-CO-001), analytics wired (`web-analytics`), and the fact-sheet claim-trace re-run against the live marketing pages (G-PR-062).

## Failure handling

- **A gate fails:** the owning step fixes the cause and re-runs the gate. Never edit the gate, weaken the check, or mark it passed in `progress.md` without the run. The same failure twice with the same approach → stop retrying and follow §6.3 (log the blocker in `progress.md`, continue all unblocked work, batch blockers into one message with a concrete option each).
- **Billing gate fails in test mode (e.g. G-IN-011):** billing does not ship. Ship everything else only if the user agrees to the §6.3 step 4 option "defer billing, ship free tier"; otherwise the release waits. Never debug billing against live keys.
- **Two skills contradict** (e.g. D12 budget vs D7 CSP headers): §5.7 precedence decides — security (rank 1) beats performance (rank 12) — and the conflict is logged in `DECISIONS.md`. Precedence never excuses skipping a gate; the gate is re-run against the winning rule.
- **A gate is itself wrong** (tests a feature the product does not have, or contradicts another gate): record a waiver in `progress.md` and `DECISIONS.md` — which gate, why it cannot pass, what was checked instead — and flag it as a repo gap (§6.3 step 5). Waivers on security, legal, or Real Content gates need the user's explicit agreement.
- **A secret leaks** (pasted in chat, committed, logged): tell the user immediately to revoke/rotate it, name the exact secret, and record the incident (name + date + rotation status, never the value) in `progress.md` (§5.9 step 4).

## Definition of done

- Deployed on a real host at a real domain; G-DO-071 passes from outside the network; monitoring and alerts live; a staging rollback drill (G-DO-151) and a backup restore drill are on record (QB-02).
- All gates in the table above pass, with results recorded in `progress.md`; zero P0 and zero P1 defects open (QB-01).
- Billing, if in scope, verified end-to-end in test mode (purchase, decline, renewal, cancellation, webhook replay) before the user-approved live switch.
- No placeholder or fake content anywhere: G-QA-141 clean and every public claim traces to `fact-sheet.md` (G-PR-062).
- `progress.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `runbook.md`, and `handover.md` are current enough that a fresh agent could resume from them alone (§5.10).
- **Pre-provisioning complete:** where no production environment exists yet, the project may be recorded as *pre-provisioning complete* — every gate except the provisioning-waived ones green, each waived gate recorded as a provisioning waiver per §6.3, and the unblocking conditions listed in `progress.md`. The deployment requirements above remain open until the environment exists; pre-provisioning complete is not done.

## Worked mini-example

Sample project: **TaskBoard**, a team task manager with a free tier and a paid Pro plan.

1. Step 0: core bundle loaded; project scaffolded from templates; `progress.md` opened; secrets list drafted (database URL, Stripe test keys, email provider key).
2. Step 1: 24 requirements written, 9 marked Must; `fact-sheet.md` records the two plan prices and the "unlimited projects on Pro" claim with its source.
3. Step 2: system design lands on three containers (web, API, Postgres) + a worker; threat model flags tenant data leakage as the top risk → multi-tenant confirmed.
4. Step 3: schema with tenant-key on every table (G-AR-092 pass); API contract suite green (G-BE-001); cross-tenant suite proves tenant A cannot read tenant B (G-DB-051); tokens pass contrast script before the board UI is built (G-AC-011).
5. Step 4: no provider was named in requirements → agent stops and asks; user picks Stripe (Option A). Test-clock walk carries a trial through renewal, a failed payment, and cancellation (G-IN-011 pass).
6. Step 5: budgets set — 200 KB JS on the board route, LCP 2.5 s — asserted in CI (G-AN-101).
7. Step 6: processing register covers accounts, billing, and analytics; consent scan shows no tracker fires pre-consent (G-LG-041).
8. Step 7: ZAP baseline finds one medium header issue, fixed and re-scanned; secret scan over history clean (G-SE-041); placeholder sweep clean (G-QA-141).
9. Step 8: pipeline deploys to production; rollback drill in staging took 3 minutes (G-DO-151); user approves the test→live key switch from the go-live checklist.
10. Step 9: production routes indexable (G-CO-001); claim-trace re-run — every price on the pricing page matches `fact-sheet.md` and the Stripe configuration (G-PR-063). Done.

# requirements-writing

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/product-requirements/requirements-writing/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/product-requirements.md`).*

## Rules

1. **PR-061 — One obligation per requirement.** Each requirement carries exactly one "shall". A requirement containing two obligations is split into two requirements before review.
2. **PR-062 — Mandatory attributes.** Every requirement carries a unique ID, source (stakeholder need or finding), priority, rationale, and verification method. A requirement missing any attribute is incomplete and cannot be baselined.
3. **PR-063 — Vague terms need numbers.** The terms fast, user-friendly, robust, seamless, flexible, and their synonyms are banned unless the same sentence states the measurable criterion the term stands for.
4. **PR-064 — Need, not design.** Requirements state the need. An implementation choice appears only as a labeled design constraint backed by a real external constraint, which is named.
5. **PR-065 — Conflicts resolved on record.** Conflicting requirements are resolved explicitly and the resolution is recorded with its decider. Wording is never averaged to hide a conflict.
6. **PR-066 — Bidirectional traceability.** Every requirement traces back to a stakeholder need and forward to at least one design element and one acceptance test. An orphan in either direction is a defect.
7. **PR-067 — Changes are versioned.** A requirement change goes through review and appears in the version history with date and decider. A silently edited requirement is treated as new and unvalidated.
8. **PR-068 — Set-level completeness.** Before handoff, the set is checked as a whole: every stakeholder need is covered by at least one requirement, and no two requirements contradict each other.
9. **PR-069 — Verifiable by construction.** Each requirement names its verification method (test, demonstration, inspection, or analysis) at the time it is written. A requirement with no method is rewritten until it has one.
10. **PR-070 — Negative requirements are explicit.** What the system must not do — data it must not retain, behaviors it must forbid — is written as requirements, not left implied by the positive ones.
11. **PR-071 — One priority per requirement.** Each requirement carries exactly one priority from the project's scheme. A requirement marked with two priorities is resolved before handoff.

## Checklist

- [ ] Requirement lint passes with zero violations (G-PR-031).
- [ ] Every requirement carries ID, source, priority, rationale, and verification method (PR-062).
- [ ] Traceability coverage is 100% for Must requirements (G-PR-032).
- [ ] All conflicts carry a recorded resolution and decider (PR-065).
- [ ] Negative requirements are written, not implied (PR-070).
- [ ] Every change since baseline appears in the version history (G-PR-034).
- [ ] The set covers every stakeholder need (PR-068).

The sheet is written before any public copy. (`skills/product-requirements/fact-sheet/SKILL.md`; full text in `bundles/product-requirements.md`)

# system-design

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/architecture/system-design/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/architecture.md`).*

## Rules

1. **AR-001 — Containers are real.** Every container in the design corresponds to a deployable unit, data store, or external system that exists in the repo or infrastructure config. Aspirational boxes are deleted or marked as future work outside the diagram.
2. **AR-002 — Every arrow is labeled.** Each relationship between containers carries a protocol or format label (HTTPS/JSON, gRPC, AMQP, SQL). An unlabeled arrow fails review.
3. **AR-003 — Failure behavior per call.** For every cross-container call, the design states the timeout, the retry policy, and what the caller does when the callee is down. A call missing any of the three is incomplete.
4. **AR-004 — Monolith by default.** The default topology is a modular monolith. A distributed design must cite, in an ADR, the requirement that forces it (independent scaling, team autonomy, isolation) — "future scale" without a load figure does not qualify.
5. **AR-005 — One writer per store.** Each data store has exactly one owning container that writes to it. Other containers read through the owner's interface or a replicated read model, never by writing directly.
6. **AR-006 — Quality attributes first.** Decomposition starts from the stated quality attributes (scale, latency, consistency, availability, tenancy), each with a target figure where one exists. A design that names components before attributes is sent back.
7. **AR-007 — Failure in the same pass.** Timeouts, retries, backpressure, and degradation are designed in the same pass as the happy path for every flow, not retrofitted after the first outage.
8. **AR-008 — Decisions become ADRs when made.** Each significant choice in the design (topology, ownership, protocol, consistency model) gets an ADR at the moment it is made, not reconstructed at the end of the project.
9. **AR-009 — Revisit on attribute change.** The design is revisited when a quality attribute changes (a new tenancy requirement, a 10× load target), not on a calendar schedule. The triggering change is named in the review note.
10. **AR-010 — External systems are explicit.** Every external system on the diagram is named, with the direction of the integration, whether it is synchronous or asynchronous, and who owns the relationship.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every container matches a deployable unit, store, or named external system (G-AR-001).
- [ ] Every arrow carries a protocol or format label (AR-002).
- [ ] Every cross-container call states timeout, retry policy, and callee-down behavior (G-AR-003).
- [ ] Data ownership is drawn: exactly one writer per store (G-AR-004).
- [ ] A distributed topology, if any, cites its forcing requirement in an ADR (AR-004).
- [ ] Each significant decision has an ADR written when it was made (AR-008).
- [ ] External systems are named with direction and sync/async marked (AR-010).

# frontend-core

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/frontend/frontend-core/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/frontend.md`).*

## Rules

1. **FE-001 — Semantic structure first.** Landmarks, headings, and native controls come before any component styling; framework components wrap native elements, and custom widgets are the last resort. (WCPM §1 priority order, R-1.x.)
2. **FE-002 — A clickable `div` is a defect.** Anything that responds to a click is a `<button>` or `<a>` with a real href, keyboard-operable and focusable. There is no styling exception.
3. **FE-003 — Reserved media dimensions.** Every image and video ships with `width`/`height` or an `aspect-ratio` so nothing shifts after load; layout stability is part of the CLS budget, not a polish step.
4. **FE-004 — Tokens only.** No hard-coded color, spacing, radius, or duration values in page or component code — semantic tokens from design-tokens are the only source (FE-041).
5. **FE-005 — The budget is a requirement.** Each route carries a JavaScript budget and the Core Web Vitals bars at the 75th percentile. A feature that breaks the budget is redesigned or split, never shipped heavy. Thresholds are cited from the numbers registry in `gates/`, per WCPM Appendix F — not restated here or per project.
6. **FE-006 — Real imagery only.** Imagery depicts the actual product, place, or people, or is clearly generic decoration. AI artifacts in photography (malformed hands, gibberish in-image text, warped logos) are a blocker, never a shrug (DET-VIS-024).
7. **FE-007 — Render real data only.** The frontend renders data that exists: no invented logos in "trusted by" rows, no unsourced stat bands, no placeholder avatars presented as people (WCPM Appendix A data/fabrication bans, D- working IDs). A claim the data cannot support is removed, not decorated.
8. **FE-008 — In-UI copy follows the copy rules.** Interface text carries no banned filler adjectives or verification phrases (WCPM Appendix A.4/A.5 word lists, CC cures); labels name the action or the thing, in the product's own vocabulary.
9. **FE-009 — The rendering surface serves search honestly.** Titles, meta descriptions, and structured data are rendered from the page's real content (WCPM §10 rendering surface; G-SCH family is designed to pass here, content owned by D9). Metadata describing content the page does not contain is a fabrication, not SEO.
10. **FE-010 — Works degraded before it works pretty.** Every page must function at 320px wide, on keyboard alone, and with images or scripts failed, before visual enhancement is layered on. Enhancement is progressive by construction.

## Checklist

- [ ] Landmarks, headings, and native controls carry the page structure (FE-001).
- [ ] No clickable divs or spans anywhere (G-FE-002, FE-002).
- [ ] Every image/video reserves its dimensions; CLS stays within budget (FE-003).
- [ ] Lighthouse CI and bundle budget are green for this route, or the local form is recorded as a tool-form substitution (G-FE-001).
- [ ] axe-core reports zero critical violations (G-FE-002).
- [ ] No raw color/spacing/duration literals outside tokens (G-FE-003).
- [ ] Every image inspected at 100%; no AI artifacts, no fake marks (G-FE-004).
- [ ] Every rendered statistic traces to a source with a date (FE-007).

<!-- generated from skills/frontend/design-tokens/SKILL.md (pointer) -->

WCPM's colour/gradient bans (C- working IDs), the COL family, and the SPC family are prevented here, at the token layer. # api-building

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/backend/api-building/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/backend.md`).*

## Rules

1. **BE-001 — One handler pipeline.** Every handler runs in this order: authenticate → authorize (object-level) → validate against the schema → run the domain operation → serialize through the response mapper. No step is skipped or reordered.
2. **BE-002 — Persistence is the definition of done.** A write endpoint is done only when its effect survives a reload and is visible from a second session or client. A 200/201 response is not evidence of an effect.
3. **BE-003 — The server recomputes trusted values.** Amounts, prices, roles, and owner IDs are never taken from the request; they are looked up or recomputed server-side from the authenticated identity and stored data.
4. **BE-004 — The database arbitrates races.** Check-then-act sequences (stock, uniqueness, balance) run inside a transaction or behind a unique constraint. Application-level "check then write" without one is a defect.
5. **BE-005 — Idempotency keys on non-replayable writes.** POSTs that create orders, take payments, or send messages accept an `Idempotency-Key`: the server stores the key with a hash of the request and the first response, replays the stored response on retry, and rejects reuse of the key with a different body.
6. **BE-006 — Two exits only.** Every handler ends in the success serializer or the problem-details error path. There is no third response shape — no ad-hoc JSON, no plain-text errors, no 200-with-error.
7. **BE-007 — Long work returns 202.** Work that depends on a slow or third-party operation returns `202` with a status resource and continues as a background job (queues-jobs). The request never blocks on a provider.
8. **BE-008 — Serializers whitelist contract fields.** Responses are built by a mapper that exposes only the fields in the OpenAPI contract. Raw database rows or ORM entities are never serialized directly.
9. **BE-009 — The contract is the source of truth.** The OpenAPI description is written or updated with the endpoint, and contract tests run against the running service in CI. Implementation and contract may not drift silently.
10. **BE-010 — Multi-record writes are atomic.** A handler that changes more than one record commits all of them or none of them in a single transaction. A partial write left behind by an error is a defect.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every handler follows the BE-001 pipeline with no skipped step.
- [ ] Every write endpoint passes its persistence test (G-BE-002).
- [ ] No trusted value (amount, price, role, owner) is taken from the request (G-BE-004).
- [ ] Non-replayable POSTs accept and honor `Idempotency-Key` (G-BE-003).
- [ ] Check-then-act paths run in a transaction or behind a constraint (BE-004).
- [ ] Responses serialize only contract fields (BE-008).
- [ ] Contract tests are green against the running service (G-BE-001).

Whatever the proof method, the session it produces obeys this skill's rules. (`skills/backend/backend-auth/SKILL.md`; full text in `bundles/backend.md`)

# schema-design

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/database/schema-design/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/database.md`).*

## Rules

1. **DB-001 — Model from the domain.** Entities and relationships are modeled first, then mapped to tables: one table per aggregate root, relationships as foreign keys. A table that mirrors a screen or an API payload instead of the domain is redesigned before it ships.
2. **DB-002 — Invariants live in the database.** Every invariant the business depends on exists as a database constraint (`NOT NULL`, `UNIQUE`, `CHECK`, or a foreign key), not only as an application check. If the app is the only thing enforcing it, the rule is not yet implemented.
3. **DB-003 — Keys.** Every table has a primary key. Surrogate keys (UUID or identity) are the default; natural keys (email, SKU, slug) are additionally protected by a unique constraint.
4. **DB-004 — Foreign keys are complete.** Every foreign key column is indexed, and every foreign key declares explicit `ON DELETE` behavior. A foreign key with the engine default delete behavior chosen by silence is a defect.
5. **DB-005 — Money is never a float.** Money is stored as integer minor units or `numeric` with an explicit scale. `float`, `double precision`, and `real` columns never hold money.
6. **DB-006 — Time is `timestamptz`.** Timestamps are stored as `timestamptz`; local-time strings and `timestamp without time zone` are not used for recorded events.
7. **DB-007 — Normalize by default.** The schema is normalized to 3NF. Denormalization happens only for a measured read pattern, and the reason is recorded in SCHEMA.md next to the duplicated field.
8. **DB-008 — Nullability is deliberate.** Each nullable column is a decision, not a default. A nullable column whose meaning is not obvious from its name is documented in SCHEMA.md.
9. **DB-009 — Soft delete is a product decision.** Rows are hard-deleted unless a written retention rule (legal hold, audit, undo window) requires soft delete; the rule names the retention period and who can see deleted rows.
10. **DB-010 — SCHEMA.md moves with the schema.** SCHEMA.md is updated in the same change as the migration that alters the schema. A schema change whose documentation lands "later" does not merge.
11. **DB-011 — The dump is generated.** The committed schema file is produced by the migration run. It is never edited by hand to match a database.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every business invariant in the design exists as a named database constraint (DB-002, G-DB-002).
- [ ] Every table has a primary key; every natural key has a unique constraint (DB-003).
- [ ] Every foreign key column is indexed and declares ON DELETE behavior (DB-004, G-DB-001).
- [ ] No money column uses a floating-point type; timestamps are timestamptz (DB-005, DB-006, G-DB-003).
- [ ] Any denormalized field names its measured reason in SCHEMA.md (DB-007).
- [ ] SCHEMA.md and the generated schema dump are updated in this change (DB-010, DB-011, G-DB-004).

# payments

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/integrations-payments/payments/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/integrations-payments.md`).*

## Rules

1. **IN-001 — Server-computed amounts.** Amount, currency, and line items are computed server-side from the catalog, keyed by the plan or product ID the client names. A client-supplied amount is a defect, not a convenience.
2. **IN-002 — Idempotency key on every money call.** Every checkout creation, charge, and refund carries an idempotency key derived from the business operation (the order ID). A retry with the same key returns the original result and creates no second charge.
3. **IN-003 — Pending order first.** The order row is created in `pending` state before the provider session or PaymentIntent exists, and the provider object is created against that order. No provider charge exists without a local order to reconcile against.
4. **IN-004 — Card data never touches your servers.** Card entry is the provider's hosted checkout page or the provider's JS elements, so card data flows browser → provider directly (SAQ A posture). No PAN in requests to your endpoints, logs, metadata, or error reports.
5. **IN-005 — Entitlement comes from the webhook, never the redirect.** Access is granted only inside the verified webhook handler or a server-side API re-read of the payment object. The success page is a display state ("payment processing") and grants nothing, so a customer who closes the tab still receives what they paid for.
6. **IN-006 — The order records the provider's payment ID.** Every paid order stores the provider payment/intent ID and the provider-reported amount and currency. A local row marked paid with no provider ID is not a payment; it is a claim.
7. **IN-007 — Declines surface as failures.** A provider decline leaves the order unpaid, shows the customer an error with a retry path, and records the decline. A decline never renders as a confirmation, a "thank you" page, or a silent success.
8. **IN-008 — Reconcile the event before fulfilling.** Before an order is fulfilled, the webhook event is checked against the expected order: account, amount, currency, and state must all match. A signed event that names the wrong amount fulfills nothing.
9. **IN-009 — Refunds are recorded against the original payment.** A refund names the original provider payment ID, carries its own idempotency key, and updates the order row and entitlement in the same flow. Dashboard-only refunds with no local record are drift the reconciliation gate will flag.
10. **IN-010 — Scheduled reconciliation diff.** A scheduled job diffs local payment rows against the provider's payment list and repairs or alerts on every mismatch. The local table is a mirror; the provider is the source of truth for money state.
11. **IN-011 — Test mode end-to-end before live.** In provider test mode: a test-card purchase grants access, a double-submit produces one charge, a webhook replay produces one grant, and a decline card declines. Test keys and test-mode labeling never appear in production configuration.
12. **IN-012 — Integer minor units.** Amounts are stored and sent as integers in the provider's minor units (cents, not dollars) with the currency stated on every record. Floating-point money math is a defect.

## Checklist

- [ ] Amounts, currency, and line items are computed server-side from the catalog (IN-001).
- [ ] Checkout, charge, and refund calls all carry order-derived idempotency keys (IN-002, G-IN-001).
- [ ] Card data reaches only the provider — hosted page or elements; absence scan clean (IN-004, G-IN-004).
- [ ] Entitlement flips only in the webhook handler or server-side re-read (IN-005, G-IN-002).
- [ ] Every paid order stores the provider payment ID, amount, and currency (IN-006).
- [ ] Decline test card declines visibly and leaves the order unpaid (IN-007, G-IN-002).
- [ ] Reconciliation diff runs on schedule and exits zero (IN-010, G-IN-003).
- [ ] Duplicate webhook delivery produces exactly one grant (G-IN-005).

# ci-cd

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/devops-deployment/ci-cd/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/devops-deployment.md`).*

## Rules

1. **DO-001 — One pipeline definition, in the repo.** The whole pipeline lives in version-controlled workflow files (`.github/workflows/*.yml` or the platform equivalent); no build or deploy step exists only in a console, a wiki, or someone's shell history.
2. **DO-002 — Fixed stage order.** Every run executes in order: checkout → install → lint → build → unit tests → integration tests → end-to-end tests → publish artifact → deploy jobs per environment. A stage may be empty only when the project genuinely has none of that test type, recorded in progress.md.
3. **DO-003 — The pipeline triggers on push and pull request, and its checks are required.** The build/test workflow runs on every push and every pull request, and its status checks are required checks on the protected branch, so a failing run blocks merge.
4. **DO-004 — Prove the pipeline can fail.** Before the gate is trusted, open a throwaway pull request containing a deliberately failing test and confirm the check reports failure and merge is blocked; record the drill result in progress.md. Repeat after any workflow or branch-protection change.
5. **DO-005 — Build once, promote the same artifact.** The artifact deployed to production is bit-identical to the one tested in staging; deploy jobs reference it by digest or immutable version tag, never by rebuilding from source.
6. **DO-006 — Gating jobs run everything, for real.** No skipped tests, no `continue-on-error`, and no commented-out steps on any job whose check is required; a step that cannot run is fixed or the job stops being a gate and the change is recorded.
7. **DO-007 — Install from the lockfile, in CI only.** Dependencies install with the lockfile-frozen command (`npm ci`, `--frozen-lockfile`, or the ecosystem equivalent); nothing installs dependencies at container start or deploy time.
8. **DO-008 — Every deploy leaves a record.** Each deploy writes one record containing the artifact digest, the commit SHA, who or what triggered it, and the timestamp; the live revision of every environment is identifiable from these records alone.
9. **DO-009 — Dependency updates flow as automated pull requests.** Dependabot or Renovate is configured for the project's ecosystems and base images, and CI scans dependencies and images for known vulnerabilities, failing the run on critical findings.
10. **DO-010 — Workflow files are linted in CI.** The pipeline runs a workflow linter (e.g., actionlint) on its own workflow files; a lint error fails the run like any other check.
11. **DO-011 — Secrets come from the CI secret store only.** Workflow files reference secrets by name from the platform secret store; no credential value is written into a workflow file, echoed into logs, or passed to builds triggered by untrusted forks.
12. **DO-012 — Delivery is measured with the DORA four keys.** Deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change fail rate, and failed-deployment recovery time are computed from pipeline and incident records on a regular cadence and reviewed in progress.md — never estimated from memory.

## Checklist

- [ ] Pipeline definition is committed and triggers on push and pull request (DO-001, DO-002).
- [ ] Build/test checks are required on the protected branch (DO-003).
- [ ] Broken-test drill performed and recorded after the last workflow or protection change (DO-004).
- [ ] Staging and production deploy records show the identical artifact digest (DO-005).
- [ ] No `continue-on-error`, skipped tests, or commented-out steps on gating jobs (DO-006).
- [ ] Dependencies install from the lockfile in CI; nothing installs at container start or deploy time (DO-007).
- [ ] Last three deploys each resolve to digest, commit SHA, actor, and timestamp (DO-008).
- [ ] Automated dependency-update pull requests are flowing and the CI vulnerability scan is green (DO-009).

## Gate criteria digest — every gate this playbook cites

Generated from the owning skills: each cited gate's Check criterion, condensed to its first sentence(s) where long, and its Pass criterion complete and exact. Fail actions and full procedures live in the owning skill and in the department bundles. This digest ships at every rung — it is what makes this bundle the default complete load for the walk (BOOTSTRAP.md step 3).

### requirements-writing (`skills/product-requirements/requirements-writing/SKILL.md`)

- **G-PR-031 — Requirement lint.** Check: automated — run a script over the requirements file confirming (a) ID, source, priority, rationale, and verification method are present and non-empty for 100% of requirements, (b) each requirement contains exactly one "shall", and (c) every banned vague term is flagged unless its sentence contains a number or unit. Pass: zero violations.
- **G-PR-032 — Traceability coverage.** Check: automated — generate the coverage report: every Must-priority requirement has at least one linked source need and at least one linked acceptance criterion or test. Pass: 100% coverage.

### fact-sheet (`skills/product-requirements/fact-sheet/SKILL.md`)

- **G-PR-063 — Price mirror diff.** Check: automated — diff the sheet's prices and plan names against the billing configuration export. Pass: zero differences.
- **G-PR-062 — Claim-trace audit.** Check: semi-automated — extract quantitative claims from shipped copy with a script, sample 10, and resolve each against a sheet entry with an evidence link. Pass: 10 of 10 trace.
- **G-PR-061 — Template completeness.** Check: automated — run a script over fact-sheet.md confirming all fixed sections are present, the limitations section is non-empty, an owner is named, and the review date is in the future. Pass: all four conditions true.

### system-design (`skills/architecture/system-design/SKILL.md`)

- **G-AR-001 — Container-to-deployable walk.** Check: manual — walk the container diagram element by element against the repo's deployable units and infrastructure config; every element must match a real unit, store, or named external system, and every relationship line in the diagram source must carry a protocol label (checked here, by eye, because label syntax differs across diagram formats). Pass: zero unmatched elements and zero unlabeled relationships.
- **G-AR-002 — Design document completeness.** Check: automated — a script confirms ARCHITECTURE.md contains a container section and that every ADR file it references exists under `docs/decisions/`. Pass: script exits 0.

### stack-selection (`skills/architecture/stack-selection/SKILL.md`)

- **G-AR-023 — Criteria predates decision.** Check: manual — in git history, confirm the criteria table exists at or before the commit that records the decision, the table scores every candidate on the same criteria, and the ADR names a rejected alternative and accepted downsides. Pass: all three hold.

### owasp (`skills/security/owasp/SKILL.md`)

- **G-SE-003 — Top 10 checklist review.** Check: manual, checklist-driven — walk the release's Top 10 record line by line; each category shows a control, a code/config location, a test, and versioned ASVS IDs where cited. Pass: all ten categories complete, N/A entries carry written reasons.
